paper_name: Direct Tax Laws and International Taxation
author: Rahul kp
title: Exemption vs
simple_words: Exemption keeps income out of the computation. Deduction cuts income after it is counted in Gross Total Income.

definitions.meaning: An income that the Act says is not taxed, so it is left out of total income and does not enter Gross Total Income.
An amount allowed under Chapter VI-A that is subtracted from Gross Total Income to reach Total Income.

key_points: ==Exemption== works first: the income is excluded, so it is never in GTI.
==Deduction== works later: income is first included in GTI, then Chapter VI-A is subtracted.
Both reduce tax, but at different stages of the computation.
!!Chapter VI-A deductions cannot exceed GTI!! and are not given against exempt income.
formula_hook: spot the stage, spot the type

insight.text: Exemption removes the income itself; deduction removes an amount from GTI that already includes the income.

memory_trick.explanation: Exempt income exits at the door and never enters GTI. Deduction is a guest already inside who leaves later, through Chapter VI-A.

steps: Add heads and set off losses: GTI
exam_tip: In a computation, never show exempt income in GTI, and never subtract Chapter VI-A items before arriving at GTI.

doubt.question: Is a rebate also a deduction?
doubt.answer: No. Deduction reduces income. Rebate reduces the tax itself, after tax is computed on Total Income.

mistakes.wrong: Including exempt income in GTI and then deducting it under Chapter VI-A
mistakes.right: Exempt income is excluded at the head level and never enters GTI.

mistakes.wrong: Deducting Chapter VI-A items from each head of income
mistakes.right: Chapter VI-A deductions are subtracted from Gross Total Income, not from individual heads.

mistakes.wrong: Treating rebate as a deduction from income
mistakes.right: Rebate is a reduction in tax payable, not in income.

applicability: Income-tax Act, 1961 as applicable for A.Y. 2026-27
reviewer_note: Chapter VI-A deductions are largely unavailable under the new regime (section 115BAC); the note speaks of the general scheme. Consider adding that caveat. Example 80C is old-regime only.
check_notes: Writer: Chapter VI-A deductions are largely unavailable under the new regime (section 115BAC); the note speaks of the general scheme. Consider adding that caveat. Example 80C is old-regime only.

Checker 1: Table row 4 (Example – Deduction: 'Donation, 80C investment') and key points 2–4: these only apply under the old regime. For A.Y. 2026-27 the default is the new regime u/s 115BAC(1A), which does not allow most Chapter VI-A deductions, including 80C and 80G; under it, only a few, such as 80CCD(2) and 80JJAA, are allowed. Add a line: 'Deductions like 80C/80G are available only if the assessee opts out of the new regime u/s 115BAC.'

Checker 1: Table row 5 (Effect – Exemption: 'Income never taxed'): this is too absolute for agricultural income. For individuals/HUFs it is still counted for rate purposes under partial integration. Suggested wording: 'Income excluded from total income (agricultural income may still affect the rate through partial integration).'

Checker 1: Key point 4: 'cannot exceed GTI' is correct u/s 80A(2). For completeness, also say that Chapter VI-A deductions are not allowed against certain incomes inside GTI, such as STCG u/s 111A, LTCG u/s 112/112A and winnings u/s 115BB.
